title: Polynomial action relations reduce coefficients to the base ring
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and let S be an R-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], generated by elements x_1, ..., x_n. Let N be an S-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] generated by e_1, ..., e_m subject to relations x_i e_j = sum_k a_{ijk} e_k with a_{ijk} in R. Then every element of N is an R-linear combination of e_1, ..., e_m.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0561, proof: the paragraph beginning “Suppose z = \sum b_j y_j” and its degree-lowering induction

proof.text:
Fix $z\in N$. Since the specified $e_1,\ldots,e_m$ generate $N$ over $S$, [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] gives $z=\sum_{j=1}^m b_je_j$ with $b_j\in S$. The specified $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ generate $S$ as an $R$-algebra, so [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] writes each $b_j$ as a polynomial in them: $b_j=\sum_
u r_{j,
u}x^
u$, where $r_{j,
u}\in R$, $
u\in\mathbf N^n$, $x^
u=\prod_i x_i^{
u_i}$, and only finitely many coefficients occur. Scalars from $R$ act through the given map $R	o S$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0561 (lemma-finitely-presented-over-subring), proof, paragraph beginning “Suppose $z = \sum b_j y_j$”

proof.text:
Induct on $d=\sum_i
u_i$, simultaneously for every generator index $j$, to show that $x^
u e_j$ is an $R$-linear combination of the $e_k$. For $d=0$, $x^
u=1$, and $e_j=\sum_k\delta_{jk}e_k$. If $d>0$, choose $i$ with $
u_i>0$ and write $
u=\mu+\epsilon_i$. The action relation and the module identities give $x^
u e_j=x^\mu(x_i e_j)=\sum_k a_{ijk}(x^\mu e_k)$. Here $\sum_i\mu_i=d-1$, so each summand has the required expression by the induction hypothesis. A finite sum of such expressions, multiplied by coefficients in $R$, is again an $R$-linear combination. This is the explicit degree-lowering induction in Tag 0561.
